I have been doing Ketovore since November 2024 when I received a call from my pcp's office informing me that I am pre-diabetic. Mind you, I had to ask for a fasting glucose, fasting insulin, and A1C test.

I had also been diagnosed with metabolic fatty liver the year before.
I have made significant changes to my nutrition, and have lost nearly thirty pounds and am healing my liver.

I am going in for labs again at the end of the month to chart my progress. Oh, according to my last liver ultrasound + fibroscan, my fatty liver is minimal, and there is no scarring - thank God!                                   

 In one year my A1C has shifted from 5.9 to 5.7, so there is some progress.
My cholesterol is 222 which has my endocrinologist pushing statins even though my Triglyceride/HDL ratio is under 1.0 which is considered excellent metabolic health and my Calcium Arterial score is ZERO which cannot be any better!

I'm a 62 year old woman, and now I'm going to start method #4 to get my body into a state of deep ketosis. My depression is much better, which I believe getting my Vit. D level up to 79 has helped significantly. I take 10K - 15K daily.

But, most importantly has been the spiritual discipline that I have added since last June: working diligently at Bible study most every day. Becoming more keenly aware of truth in this human experience is revolutionary; and, taking ownership of my health (all categories) is healing and life changing!

My greatest takeaway from the various doctors that I have is the complete lack of Curiousity that they gave of my progress! As one doctor told me -- medicine has become a business. 

Thanks for sharing your journey with us, Kerry!

PURE MEAT AS IT COMES FROM THE  ANIMAL  with as much fat as that animal carries on,  and in,😮 its flesh ..and water .. no more , no less..  keep your brain focused on the task ahead and rest when you can .

top_comments.text:
I just thought I'd share this because Dr. Baker was talking about marathon running and saying he wasn't completely sure how a carnivore athlete would perform at that level over long distances.

All I can do is speak from my own experience.

For people who don't know motocross, it's hard to explain just how physically demanding it really is. It's widely considered one of the toughest sports in the world because there are no breaks. No timeouts. No substitutions. No jogging down the court while the play develops. Once that gate drops, it's full intensity until the checkered flag.

Professional motocross races are 30 minutes plus 2 laps, and that doesn't sound crazy until you realize you're wrestling a 250-pound motorcycle with over 60 horsepower underneath you the entire time. Every bump, rut, braking bump, jump, landing, acceleration zone, and corner is trying to rip the bike out of your hands.

Your heart rate is through the roof the entire moto. It's common for riders to spend long periods in the 170 to 190+ BPM range while making split second decisions at high speed. One mistake can send you flying 60 feet through the air or straight into the ground. You're not just physically exhausted, you're mentally locked in every second because if your concentration slips, you're crashing.

Then add the environment. You're wearing heavy boots, knee braces, chest protectors, helmets, goggles, gloves, and full riding gear in the middle of summer. The tracks get rougher every lap. Deep ruts form. Braking bumps get bigger. The bike gets harder to control. Yet you still have to push harder because everyone around you is doing the same thing.

When I was racing at a local pro level around 19 years old, my training was absolutely insane. Marathon distances weren't some special accomplishment to us, they were just training. I would run close to 20 miles a day Monday through Friday and still do weight training on top of that just to prepare for weekend races. That was normal. You had to build an engine capable of surviving race day because motocross will expose every weakness you have physically and mentally.

Fast forward to now. I'm 31 years old and I've been retired from racing professionally for over 10 years. For a long time I stopped training completely. I got unhealthy, gained weight, my acid reflux was horrible, my energy disappeared, and honestly I felt depressed. I was just going through the motions.

Then I came across Dr. Anthony Chaffee and Dr. Shawn Baker talking about the carnivore diet. I figured I had nothing to lose, so I went all in. No cheating, no easing into it. I cut everything out and committed to giving it an honest shot.

The first few months were rough. The keto flu hit hard. But once I got through it, everything changed. The weight came off, the acid reflux disappeared, my mental clarity came back, my energy skyrocketed, and I started feeling like myself again.

Three years later I'm still carnivore. The only plant I consume is a morning coffee with a splash of heavy cream. I fast throughout the day and usually eat one large meal until I'm full.

Recently I decided to get back on a motocross bike after about five years away from riding. No training. No running. No gym. Just diet.

I expected to get completely destroyed.

The first ride definitely humbled me and I was sore, but I was shocked at how much I could actually ride. The second ride felt better. The third ride felt even better. My recovery was faster than I expected and my conditioning started coming back quickly despite doing none of the training I used to do.

That's what really got my attention.

Coming back to one of the most physically demanding sports on earth with no training and feeling the way I did has honestly made me wonder what would happen if an elite athlete trained the way I used to train while also following a carnivore diet.

Whether it's motocross, marathon running, cycling, wrestling, or any endurance sport, I genuinely believe they could be operating on another level.

Now that's just my opinion and my personal experience. I'm not claiming everyone will have the same results. But after living both lifestyles, training extremely hard while eating whatever I wanted, and now riding again while being fully carnivore, the difference has been impossible for me to ignore.

For me, it wasn't even close.

It was night and day.

top_comments.text:
The "they just died earlier" argument doesn't hold up against consecutive year-on-year data.

Here's why:•Year-on-year increases over THE MOST REVENT 5 years can't be explained by "living slightly longer" — If it were just about increased life expectancy, you'd see a one-off jump when old data meets new methodology, not a consistent upward trend every single year.

Age-standardised rates already control for age structure — Epidemiological data usually reports age-adjusted incidence precisely to remove the confounding effect of an ageing population.

Incidence (new cases) vs survival — Higher survival from other causes would increase prevalence, but the argument falls apart when you're looking at new diagnoses rising every year across multiple demographics.

The trend is consistent across Western populations — If it were purely a historical artefact, you'd see plateauing once detection normalised. Instead, the trend continues.

5 consecutive years of rising rates = a pattern, not a statistical artefact — You can't explain away a sustained multi-year trend with better diagnostics or marginal life expectancy gains.

Bottom line: The "died before they could get it" argument might work as a partial explanation for some historical undercounting, but it completely fails to explain persistent, year-on-year increases in modern incidence data.

videos.title: Does Creatine Really Cause Hair Loss? What the Science Actually Shows
videos.channel_name: Dr. Eric Westman - Adapt Your Life
videos.description:
⭐ FREE CARNIVORE DIET WORKSHOP 17 & 19 JANUARY 2026 8PM EST ⭐ Discover the power of carnivore for autoimmune, gut, and metabolic healing. Sign up below. 👇https://adaptyourlifeacademy.kit.com/carnivore-workshop-jan-2026

A common claim online is that creatine causes hair loss or baldness  and for many people, that fear alone is enough to avoid one of the most studied supplements in the world.

In this video, I review the actual human research behind creatine, hair loss, testosterone, DHT, kidney function, uric acid, and weight gain. The concern originated from a small 2009 study that looked at DHT levels, not hair loss itself — and crucially, those findings were never replicated. Since then, more than a dozen studies have examined creatine’s effects on testosterone and DHT, with no consistent evidence linking creatine supplementation to male pattern baldness.

I also explain an important concept most people miss: confounding variables. Resistance training itself can raise testosterone and DHT, and people who take creatine are usually training harder — making creatine an easy scapegoat. The video also covers kidney health, gout concerns, water weight vs fat gain, and why creatine has been unfairly blamed despite decades of safe use.

If you’re lifting weights, following a low-carb or keto-style diet, or considering creatine for muscle preservation, performance, or aging, this breakdown will help you separate myth from measurable outcomes.

if you place an order, write Emma is so cool in the notes and I’ll include 2 free chapsticks! 
you can use code THANKS10 for 10% off your order!!

Things I used in this video:
Silicone candy bar molds: https://amzn.to/4a0SMot
Non-toxic, oven-safe stainless steel pans: https://amzn.to/3ZtSku2
ELECTROLYTE+ Flake Sea Salt: https://livesaltr.com/products/electrolyte-flake-sea-salt?variant=46746895745178
Salted Caramel Coffee Electrolyte: https://livesaltr.com/products/salted-caramel-coffee-electrolyte-drink-mix?pr_prod_strat=jac&pr_rec_id=191166f79&pr_rec_pid=8666866122906&pr_ref_pid=8675048489114&pr_seq=uniform&variant=46720172228762

How to make the three carnivore candy bars:
First, take a measuring cup and fill your molds with water so you can see exactly how much liquid your molds hold. This helps you estimate how much butter you’ll need.

100% strict carnivore version:
You need salted butter and thick sea salt. Brown your butter in a frying pan on low heat, stirring constantly until it becomes bubbly and frothy and the bottom turns caramelized. Let it cool slightly, pour into your molds, sprinkle with sea salt, and freeze for 1–2 hours or overnight.

Vanilla carnivore candy bar:
Follow the same exact steps, but add a small splash of vanilla extract to the butter before pouring into your molds.

Salted caramel coffee toffee candy bar (my favorite):
Use unsalted butter since the electrolytes already contain salt. Brown the butter the same way, then add a small pour of the salted caramel coffee electrolytes. Taste and adjust to your liking, then pour into molds and freeze.

#carnivore

videos.title: Carnivore/Lion Diet Update: Not Carnivore Anymore?
videos.description:
Huge news—I can now tolerate some plant foods without arthritis or depression flares! After 8 years of strict ruminant meat only, I have shifted to animal-based/keto (meat + greens). The lion diet achieved remission but I needed more help to add foods back in. My reactions to plant foods have been either eliminated for a lot of the plants or dramatically reduced. This is what I’ve been aiming at for years. 

Also if you do find this helpful I would love help funding the keto/carnivore study: https://gofund.me/e8ba31ba4

And please consider applying to take part in the study if you meet these criteria:

Formal medical diagnosis of IBD or RA and willing to provide paperwork of diagnosis.
Not pregnant or breastfeeding.
New to the ketogenic or lion diet.
Willing to do the ketogenic or lion diet for 3-6 months depending on random sorting.
Willing to do their regular diet for 3 months and be monitored, before starting dietary intervention, depending on random sorting.
Willing to pay $200 (and receive $100 back once the study is concluded)

Link to apply to the study:
https://l.bttr.to/mXwng

In this video I’m going to kind of haphazardly go over what I’ve been through in the last 10 years, what eventually worked to reduce “sensitivities”, and what didn’t work at all. This is not an extensive list of what didn’t work, but it is an extensive list of what did work.

If you have questions leave them below and I’ll get to them in a Q and A I’m putting out soon! 

I still 100% recommend the lion diet as a fast way to achieve remission for autoimmune or mood disorders while you figure out what your root cause is. I think a lot of people probably have similar root causes as me - mold, and gut dysbiosis that are both difficult to test for. I also know that I wouldn’t have survived long enough to figure them out without putting myself into remission with the lion diet, during this time. That may sound dramatic, but my body ate my hip and ankle when I was 17, and was breaking down the rest of my joints quickly. Death as an outcome of that is not dramatic.

Here’s an article: https://liondiet.com/no-longer-carnivore/ that basically reiterates what is in this video, and I’ll keep everyone posted on the continued health journey.

I have a ways to go to be “optimal” like biohackers (who didn’t have multiple joints replaced) are. I’m unbelievably burnt out after this year of health issues with my family, and work over the last 8 years, and medical trauma. I’m not at the point where I’m comfortable eating out. Keto for Beginners: My Simple Plate Method for Real Life Results
If you’re new to keto and overwhelmed by macros, carb counts, and endless food rules, this video is for you. In this beginner-friendly guide, I break down the simple plate method I use with patients to help them start keto in a practical, sustainable way. #keto #ketoforbeginners #lowcarb #metabolichealth #weightloss

You do not have to be carnivore to heal. For many people, keto is the perfect starting point because it lowers carbs, helps reduce cravings, improves blood sugar, and supports fat loss without making food feel too restrictive. In this video, I explain how to build a keto plate with protein first, low-carb vegetables if desired, healthy fat for satiety, and without the starches and sugars that keep people stuck.

We’ll also cover one of the biggest mistakes keto beginners make and why some people use keto as a bridge to carnivore while others stay keto long term and do great.

On this channel, we focus on the root causes of why people get sick and how real food and lifestyle changes can help them heal.

What you’ll learn:
Why keto is a powerful healing tool
The simple plate method I use with patients
How to build a keto meal without overthinking
The biggest mistake keto beginners make
Why keto can be a bridge to carnivore
How to choose the path that works best for your body

videos.title: The Hard Truth About Your First 7 Days on Carnivore
videos.description:
The Hard Truth About Your First 7 Days on Carnivore
If you’re new to keto and overwhelmed by macros, carb counts, and endless food rules, this video is for you. In this beginner-friendly guide, I break down the simple plate method I use with patients to help them start keto in a practical, sustainable way. #keto #ketoforbeginners #lowcarb #metabolichealth #weightloss

You do not have to be carnivore to heal. For many people, keto is the perfect starting point because it lowers carbs, helps reduce cravings, improves blood sugar, and supports fat loss without making food feel too restrictive. In this video, I explain how to build a keto plate with protein first, low-carb vegetables if desired, healthy fat for satiety, and without the starches and sugars that keep people stuck.

We’ll also cover one of the biggest mistakes keto beginners make and why some people use keto as a bridge to carnivore while others stay keto long term and do great.

On this channel, we focus on the root causes of why people get sick and how real food and lifestyle changes can help them heal.

What you’ll learn:
Why keto is a powerful healing tool
The simple plate method I use with patients
How to build a keto meal without overthinking
The biggest mistake keto beginners make
Why keto can be a bridge to carnivore
How to choose the path that works best for your body
Resources:

Check out my links, books, and educational resources here:
Dr. Tony Hampton Linktree

Watch next:
Carnivore for Beginners: The First 7 Days
How to Adopt a Low-Carb Diet
How to Start a Carnivore Journey

#DrTonyHampton #keto #ketodiet #ketoforbeginners #lowcarblifestyle #bloodsugar #insulinresistance #weightlossjourney #metabolichealth #carnivorediet

Pinned comment

You do not have to be carnivore to heal.

Where are you watching from, and are you more keto, carnivore, or somewhere in between?

top_comments.text: I grew up in the desert southwest. Take a cold bath; it will drop your core body temperature. If it's too hot to sleep, wearing a wet t-shirt with a fan blowing on you will help you get to sleep. Don't worry, the shirt and bed will be dry by morning. Reusable ice packs for coolers put into a cloth behind your neck and on your wrists will help cool your body down. Take one to bed. Ceiling fans will help cool a room better than a floor fan. A fan in the window venting hot air outside can really help reduce the heat inside. Try to keep windows with the sun hitting them closed. If possible, block the sun from hitting the window and heating it up. I put a blind outside the window. Or keep the drapes closed when the sun hits the window. There are portable AC units that don't need to be installed in a window, just vented out the window with an attachment. If you can get one room that's cool to sleep in, that will make a difference. Best of luck to you. The heat can be brutal. （＾∀＾●）ﾉｼ

videos.title: You'll Never Eat Sardines Again
videos.description:
🥩 Get The FREE Animal-Based Diet Guide: https://www.paulsaladinomd.com/animal-based-diet

Find out your ideal diet with my ANIMAL-BASED CALCULATOR: https://www.paulsaladinomd.co/ab-guide#calculator?utm_source=youtube&utm_medium=video&utm_campaign=VIDEOID

--- --- ---

Sardines are often marketed as a “superfood,” and the sardine fast has recently gone viral online as a way to lose weight and improve metabolic health. But are sardines actually safe to eat regularly? In this video, Dr. Paul Saladino investigates the potential dangers of sardines, including concerns around contaminants, packaging, and why relying on a single food like sardines during a “sardine diet” may not be as harmless as many people think.

I break down what’s really happening with the sardine fast trend, why some sardines may contain problematic compounds, and what people should understand before making them a daily staple. And if you do choose to eat sardines, I explain how to minimize potential risks by choosing better sources and preparing them properly, so you can make more informed decisions about this popular food.

--- --- ---

If you can't get fresh heart & liver in your diet, try our 100% grass-fed desiccated beef organs at Heart & Soil: https://shop.heartandsoil.co/?utm_source=youtube&utm_medium=video&utm_campaign=VIDEOID

Looking for a healthy and delicious snack? 
This is why I created Lineage Provisions. Giving you real foods in the most convenient way. Check us out: http://lineageprovisions.com/psmdyt


--- --- ---
RESEARCH:

Heavy Metals

Souza et al., 2022 – Journal of Food Composition and Analysis. Analysis of 120 canned sardine samples found arsenic levels associated with hazard quotients and carcinogenic risk estimates above safety thresholds. https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC9266115/

ConsumerLab Testing (2020, 2025). Independent testing detected arsenic in canned sardines, with several products exceeding 100 mcg per serving. 

Food Chemistry Study (2024). Reported most sardine samples tested exceeded maximum permissible arsenic limits.

Shiber, 2010 – Marine Pollution Bulletin. Mercury not detected, but arsenic, cadmium, and lead were present in canned sardines.

Hong Kong Consumer Council (2019). Cadmium detected in most sardine samples; some also contained dioxin-like PCBs.

Packaging / BPA

Canadian Survey (2015). BPA detected in canned sardines with high levels of bioaccessibility.

EFSA (2023). Reduced tolerable daily intake of BPA by 20,000× due to immune system concerns.

McGill University Research (2025). BPA replacements such as BPS can leach from packaging and may have similar biological effects.

Oxidation

Lipid oxidation studies on canned fish show EPA and DHA degrade over time, with oxidation markers increasing during storage.

Research on cholesterol oxidation products shows higher levels in canned fish stored in brine compared to oil.

Histamine

Tehran Market Study found some canned sardine samples exceeding FDA histamine limits, with histamine levels that cannot be reduced by canning.

Microplastics

International analysis of canned sardine brands detected plastic particles in several products.

Cal State Fullerton (2021) confirmed microplastic contamination in canned sardines.

top_comments.text:
Interesting perspective, but some of these arguments feel overly alarmist and slightly outdated, especially depending on where you live.
First, the heavy metal warning is largely misplaced. Sardines are at the very bottom of the food chain, meaning they don't accumulate mercury like large predators (e.g., tuna or swordfish). As for the arsenic mentioned, the type naturally found in marine life is predominantly arsenobetaine (organic arsenic), which is non-toxic and easily excreted by the human body.
Second, the BPA argument is quickly becoming a thing of the past. For instance, the EU introduced a strict ban on BPA in food contact materials that took full effect in early 2025. The vast majority of modern cans on the European market now use BPA-NI (Non-Intent) linings, making the endocrine disruptor risk practically negligible.
I definitely agree with your point about choosing sardines in water/brine over those packed in cheap seed oils! However, eating canned sardines in water 3x a week is perfectly safe. It remains one of the most affordable, nutrient-dense sources of Omega-3s (EPA/DHA), highly bioavailable calcium, and protein. There's really no need to fear-monger such a great whole food.

top_comments.text:
I always tell my female clients that "heavy" means something different for everyone. When I started eating carnivore, I weighed 265 pounds and was very out of shape. Even a 5-pound dumbbell felt difficult, and everyday things like bending over or climbing stairs left me exhausted. Now I can comfortably lift 25-pound dumbbells. That might not seem heavy to everyone—my husband can lift much more—but that small increase, along with eating carnivore, completely changed my body. I now weigh 155 pounds.

You don't have to feel exhausted, sore, or miserable when exercising. I have friends who do nothing but roller skate, and they look like athletes. If you can't do a 15-minute bodyweight workout with good form, there's no need to add weights yet. If you're overweight, your body itself is already resistance. People often say "lift heavy," but they don't explain that, so I hope this is helpful. If your goal is maximum muscle growth as quickly as possible, such as for a vacation or competition, then lifting very heavy and training to failure can help. But if your goal is simply to be slim and toned, you don't have to do that. Walking regularly and eating enough protein can naturally help shape your body. I've heard so many carnivore ladies, even the older ladies, say that they slimmed down and got "curvy" but they don't workout at all.

One of my biggest tips for anyone starting carnivore is to use a measuring tape or a waist trainer instead of relying only on the scale. For months, my weight barely changed. Some days I was down five pounds, and the next day I might be up eight pounds, which was frustrating. But I kept tightening my waist trainer and eventually had to buy a smaller size. My husband noticed I felt much smaller, even when I couldn't see the difference myself. At first, the only changes I noticed was that my acne disappeared, and weirdly my nails became stronger and really long. I literally was complaining because I accidently kept scratching us both while sleeping lol. my mood improved. I felt happier, calmer, and less anxious. By the end of the summer, I went shopping for holiday clothes and automatically headed to the plus-size section like I always had. To my surprise, the clothes were too big. I left the store flabbergasted with medium-sized clothes.
top_comments.author: @bre6651

videos.title: Why Steak Is at the Top | Dr. Shawn Baker
videos.channel_name: American Thought Leaders - The Epoch Times
videos.description:
🔵 Support independent journalism and subscribe to The Epoch Times now for just $1 per week: https://theepochtim.es/ATLUSA

Canada Edition: https://theepochtim.es/ATLCA

🔵 Sign up for the American Thought Leaders ALERTS newsletter to stay up-to-date on new episodes, releases, and special events 👉 https://ept.ms/ATLnewsletter

HHS Secretary Robert F. Kennedy recently unveiled a new food pyramid and dietary guidelines for Americans that emphasize high-quality protein, dairy, healthy fats, vegetables, and fruits. Whole grains are downgraded, and processed foods and added sugars are discouraged.

“We've been consuming this ultra-processed food, which I call human pet food,” says Dr. Shawn Baker. A former orthopedic surgeon and world champion athlete, he’s the author of “The Carnivore Diet” and co-founder of the online clinic Revero.

“A lot of our food has become very similar to recreational drugs in the way we use and abuse them,” he says.

Eating a lot of addictive, ultra-processed food—high in carbs, sugars, and seed oils—drives inflammation and can lead to obesity, diabetes, arthritis, cardiovascular problems, gut malfunction, depression, and cancers, he explains.

In our in-depth interview, he explains how and why the adoption of low-carb, high-fat diets reduces inflammation and can even reverse chronic diseases such as diabetes and cardiometabolic disease.

There is even significant evidence that such diets can be used therapeutically for neurological and mental health issues, he says.

One of those low-carb, high-fat diets is the ketogenic diet. But what happens when you take keto one step further and go on the carnivore diet?

“Carnivore is basically a diet consisting primarily of animal products. So it would be meat. It would be fish. It would be eggs. It would be dairy products,” he says. This means no plant products at all.

The carnivore diet is not for everyone, but many people suffering from debilitating autoimmune diseases have healed themselves with such a diet, he says. Mikhaila Peterson has famously documented her transformative experience on an even more restricted version of this diet called the “lion diet.”

In our in-depth interview, we discuss many more questions regarding food as medicine and the benefits of a protein-heavy diet, including:

- Why people on ketogenic or carnivore diets experience something called ‘keto calm’ or ‘zero carb zen.’
- Why going on the carnivore diet does not harm your nutritional intake, contrary to what many may think.
- Why such diets can help reverse inflammatory bowel disease, Tourette syndrome, and hypermobility, also known as Ehlers-Danlos syndrome.

It’s time for Americans to stop simply relying on America’s “disease management system” of drugs and pharmaceuticals, he argues, and instead take their health into their own hands.

Views expressed in this video are opinions of the host and the guest, and do not necessarily reflect the views of The Epoch Times.

videos.title: Why I Don't Want To Be Carnivore
videos.description:
I’m not quitting the carnivore diet.
I’m not anti carnivore, anti meat, or anti protein.
And I’m writing a carnivore diet cookbook with carnivore recipes for all of you!

The honest truth is… I don’t want to eat this way.

I want pizza. I want desserts. I want comfort food.
But I choose to eat carnivore most of the time because my body and my brain work better when I do.

This livestream is about the difference between what we want and what we choose. And I'm not going to lie and pretend to be a perfect carnivore influencer to show off my elite carnivore lifestyle that doesn't exist. It's not about perfection for me.

It’s about:
• Doing carnivore for health, not trends
• Why diet tribalism hurts real people
• Being honest about discipline and flexibility
• Not fitting perfectly into any diet group
• Using food to support focus, mood, and energy
• Choosing progress over perfection

If you’ve ever felt judged, confused, or out of place in diet culture — this stream is for you.

I believe in carnivore.
I’m living it.
I’m building recipes around it.
But I don’t believe in turning diets into religions.

I believe in real people trying to get healthier one decision at a time.

👇 Join the conversation in the comments.

Eat your meat, love your life (even if some days you don't really want to).

- Chris

top_comments.text:
I lost about 100 lbs on Keto-Ketovore. I'm 64, 5.9 and now 150 lbs. I did carnivore, and still mostly do in addition to OMAD (usually). What I personally found about carnivore was that it is, IMO, overly restrictive in a few ways.

First, yes, you can have some veggies, in moderation, particularly if they do not bloat you. No, I don't feel guilty having a bit of broccoli or spinach on the side of my ribeye. You can also have some nuts (check the label); almonds and walnuts are very good, again, in moderation. Almost no carbs, good fat/protein ratio. You can make such small compromise and enjoy your carnivore diet more.

Second, take a multi-vitamin and cover all your bases nutritionally. Yes, they say you get everything on carnivore...still, back it up. There's no reason not to.

Third, in spite of many YT videos, you do NOT need to resort to eating whole sticks of butter and the like. Further, carnivore leads to decreased appetite, so listen to your body, and eat only when your hungry, and when you do eat, do so slowly, enjoy the meal, and stop when you're full...don't stuff yourself because you think you can.

Last, sadly but true, you MUST give up alcohol if its going to work, because your body won't burn the fat you intake on carnivore while it's dealing with clearing out the toxin.

My biggest take-away was that it ie very effective and much more healthy than almost any diet solution; and a very healthy lifestyle. But, you don't need to put on blinders and freak at the prospect of having a few minor deviations. And yes, our "ancestors" ate wild berries and nuts from trees. They didn't just hunt, they also "gathered"--so a bit of moderation is just fine...just no compromise on sugar/starches/processed foods/alcohol. Dairy, as this man points out, is a very individualistic thing, so however you find it works in or doesn't is something to experiment with.

ZERO CARB PANCAKES... made with EGGS? 🥞🥚

Most low-carb pancake recipes depend on almond flour, coconut flour, or cream cheese. These Keto Pancakes take a completely different approach.

✅ 1 Ingredient + 2 Functional Properties
✅ No almond flour
✅ No coconut flour
✅ No grains
✅ No starches
✅ High protein

The secret is food science.

Whipped egg whites create lift and volume. Beef gelatin helps stabilize the structure. Powdered sweetener improves protein stability and elasticity during whipping.

The result? Light, airy Keto Pancakes that absorb butter and sugar-free syrup beautifully without the dense or gritty texture found in many low-carb pancakes.

If you've been looking for a simple keto breakfast that's fast, easy, and incredibly satisfying, this recipe might surprise you.

top_comments.text: Thank you doctor Petrilla!!! This video is just what I needed to hear! When I started Carnivore, It was out of desperation. Doctors had not been any help to me, but had hurt me for over 20 years. It took every bit of 2 years of meat and fat, to heal my body enough to include some veggies and fruits back. I started carbs back, because while Carnivore was a necessity, it couldn't be my lifestyle. When I added some veggies back, the impact was immediate, I felt better instantly and my body responded positively in ways I didn't even think possible. So while I still eat a meat and fat heavy diet, I add cooked veggies and certain fruits. I've learned through trial and error, that sugars/fructose/glucose are my problem, they cause me severe inflammation, and too much high oxalate veggies cause me some issues. When I was a Carnivore, I struggled with oxalate dumping, that frankly was exhausting to deal with, but adding some veggies with low to medium oxalate content, helped me out tremendously. My body stopped all the dumping. I try not to put more of it in than my body can clean out, but I'm sure I screw up, lol! Since I can't eat dairy anymore, I rely heavily on coconut cream to fill that gap. I love the stuff. I love coconut pancakes, egg yolk cake, with coconut cream frosting and I especially love coconut cream ice cream pops, on those hot days, and I get a satisfying protein and fat boost. I make them as healthy as I can, adding egg yolks to the coconut cream, and collagen peptides, coconut flakes and toasted almonds. Almonds are the only nut that I can eat, so far as I know. But I soak the raw nuts in filtered water for 24 hours in a salt brine, rinse them well, then roast them until crunchy. I eat them only as a garnish for fruit or a coconut dessert. I've just added cooked mushrooms to my diet today, I'll see how it goes, if I have any reactions it will have to go. There are some fruits and veggies that I will not be able to eat, and I'm fine with that. As long as what I do eat, aids my body in better function and health, then that's what I will live on. TY for your insights, they help me now that I'm not lost in this better health endeavor. 🥰😘

Blood donations confound the ferritin result. Ferritin dropped 325→165. Blood donation directly removes iron. This is an independent intervention with its own cardiovascular effects 
(reduced blood viscosity, hematocrit, oxidative load). The dietary change cannot be credited for the ferritin improvement.

 "quit alcohol after 20 years of drinking."
This is a massive uncontrolled variable that is completely unaddressed in the analysis.
Alcohol cessation alone produces well-documented lipid effects:

Triglycerides drop significantly — alcohol is a direct driver of hypertriglyceridemia via hepatic VLDL overproduction
Blood pressure decreases — alcohol is dose-dependently hypertensive; 20 years of heavy drinking would have established persistent elevation
Liver function improves — hepatic lipid metabolism normalizes, which directly affects LDL particle production and clearance, thyroid hormone conversion (T4→T3 is liver-dependent), and ferritin levels (alcohol drives ferritin elevation independently of dietary iron)

A quick tour of the plant-based "milks" that were going to save you and the planet.

Almond milk. Ingredients: water, almonds (2%), calcium carbonate, sunflower lecithin, locust bean gum, gellan gum, potassium citrate, dipotassium phosphate, sea salt, natural flavour, vitamin mix. Each litre uses around 1,600 gallons of irrigated water in a state that has been in drought for a decade.

Oat milk. Ingredients: water, oats, rapeseed oil, dipotassium phosphate, calcium carbonate, tricalcium phosphate, sea salt, riboflavin, vitamin A, D2, B12. Hexane-extracted seed oil with a dusting of grain in it. Spikes your blood sugar like a can of Coke.

Soy milk. The soy was grown for the oil. The leftover meal, normally fed to pigs and chickens, is what you are drinking. The industrial by-product of seed oil production, sold to you as the ethical choice.

Coconut milk. Thickened with carrageenan, shown in studies to provoke gut inflammation. Driving deforestation across Southeast Asia. Some Thai producers still use chained monkey labour to harvest the coconuts.

Rice milk. Ingredients: water, rice, sunflower oil, calcium carbonate, sea salt, gellan gum, locust bean gum, vitamins. Sugar water with a faint memory of rice and another splash of seed oil for good measure.

Pea milk. Engineered in a lab in 2015. Ingredients: water, pea protein isolate, sunflower oil, cane sugar, calcium phosphate, sea salt, gellan gum, xanthan gum, sunflower lecithin, natural flavour. The contents of a chemistry set in a carton.

Hemp milk. Tastes like a barn floor. Still contains sunflower lecithin and gellan gum, because nothing in this aisle is allowed to exist without an emulsifier.

Cashew milk. The shells contain a chemical so caustic that the women in Vietnam who hand-process them routinely suffer permanent skin damage. The world's most exploitative latte.

Cow's milk. Ingredients: cow's milk.

Eight thousand years on the table. No marketing budget required.
top_comments.author: @dsampey222

top_comments.text: Saturated fat is not the enemy... "For 50 years, the dietary establishment has told us that saturated fat is the road to cardiovascular death. France didn't get the memo. Annual per capita consumption: - Butter: ~8 kg per person, among the highest in the world - Cheese: ~27 kg per person, the highest in the world - Cream, foie gras, duck fat, lard, rillettes: woven into the daily diet - Saturated fat: roughly 15% of total calories, well above official guidelines French cardiovascular mortality: among the lowest in the developed world. French obesity rate: around 17%. The US: around 42%. French life expectancy: roughly 82-83 years. The official explanation is "the French paradox," which is the term experts reach for when the data refuses to do what the model says it should. It isn't a paradox. It's what happens when a population eats real food, mostly cooked at home, mostly from animals that lived properly, with the saturated fat intact and the seed oils kept out of the kitchen. The French eat butter on bread, not margarine. They cook in duck fat, not sunflower oil. They drink wine with dinner, not Diet Coke. They sit down for an actual meal instead of grazing on snack bars between meetings. The paradox is the model. The French are just eating like humans."
top_comments.author: @bellaholden4530

top_comments.text:
Couple things to add to this conversation on some possibilities as to why some do better on dairy than others....

1. 90% of cheese made in the U.S. is either a Pfizer mold based processed rennet or vegetable enzymes.
So, if you are sensitive to mold or oxylates, eating cheese thats not made from animal rennet might be an issue.

2. Milk products. There's two types of milk, A1 & A2. Most milk products are made with A1. 
"A1 milk contains the amino acid histidine at position 67, while A2 contains proline. This tiny change affects digestion and how your body reacts to the dairy."

3. Butter. Most brands are a combination of A1 milk and seed oils they dont list on the label. So, sensitive tummys might have a problem. 
The safest butter is Kerry Gold.

Lastly, let's not forget many of these heavy creams have questionable ingredients like polysorbate 80 and carrageene.

So, if you question any of these, read your labels. Dont buy products with questionable ingredients. Contact the manufacturer and inquire. Its the only way to know.

PS..

If a dairy company uses hoilstein cows, they produce A1 milk. 
If they have jersey or Guernsey, its A2.

Hope this was helpful for folks.

Great video and excellent graphics. I’m struggling, however, with the logic regarding the CAC score dichotomy. If we hypothesize that high ApoB is not inherently damaging for those with the LMHR phenotype, why does a non-zero CAC score change that assessment?

It seems more plausible that existing calcification is a 'legacy' marker—damage set in motion before the individual adopted the diet that triggered their LMHR profile. density lipoproteins (LDL), medium/intermediate density (IDL), and
high density (HDL). Every lipoprotein contains either an ApoA “tag”
or an ApoB tag. ApoA attaches itself to HDL, and ApoB attaches
itself to LDL. The cells that require cholesterol absorb the ApoB
containing lipoproteins on the way through the bloodstream, bind
them up on the cell membrane, and pump as much cholesterol out
of the lipoprotein into the cell as is required. That’s the process in a
nutshell.
The sugar molecules involved in the heart disease process bind
to proteins on the cholesterol carried by LDL and sdLDL particles
(smaller versions of LDL) via glycation, as previously alluded to.
Fructose has a much higher glycation rate as well. When they bind
to the molecules, they derange the receptor that allows your liver to
take them in (the ApoB 100 receptor). When this gets “knocked out,”
so to speak, the only thing that can sequester them are the
scavenger receptors on your macrophages. They continue to engulf
them because they have an unlimited capacity to do so, and
therefore form large “foam cells.” Once you have damage to your
arterial walls, which is required for the process of heart disease, then
those molecules will invaginate into the defect, and will then help to
form atherosclerotic plaque. The lipoproteins do not get deposited
into the arterial walls without these defects. In other words, if you
don’t have damage to the arterial walls of the blood vessels, this will
not happen."

THE 4 CLAIMS ADDRESSED IN THIS VIDEO:
1.	"Fiber is essential" → Technically not. No fiber deficiency syndrome defined. Beneficial for many, not essential for everyone.

THE BIGGER PRINCIPLE: Follow outcomes, not ideology.

top_comments.text:
Have you lost any weight since you started the ketovore diet? 
I stalled on carnivore, then stalled on ketovore/living carnivore and started adjusting my time of eating along with fasting.  
I have visceral fat around my waist and  wanted to shrink it way down. The amount of average sized (not considered fat) people that carry around dangerous amounts of visceral fat is more than one would think. 
To much visceral fat can also affect hormones and cause other health issues, even autoimmune problems.  
It is actually harder to get rid of than just losing weight. But losing weight does slowly get rid of it.  It was taking to long for me,  after 2 yrs at it,  I needed to move that progress quicker. 
Anyways,  I started this way of eating a month ago and the visceral fat is finally reacting, and coming off at a nice pace as is the weight.  I'm just using a tape measure to measure around the belly button to figure out an idea of how much visceral around the waist.  There are formulas as well.  This is my diet schedule:  
At noon: I eat 1 lb of ground hamburger and 4 eggs with 1/2 cup of fermented sauerkraut. 
I can only eat half,  so I wait about 2 hrs and finish the second half.  So my eating window is 2 hrs.  
I switch up 1 lb of steak instead of 1 lb hamburger every other day as a variety.  In the morning around 10am I have a mug of green tea only.  I put nothing else with it.  Just tea bags.  
With my meal and the rest of the day I only drink plain water.  So the one big meal split up within a  2 hrs window and I don't eat again until noon the next day.  
I do not snack at all...that stops your fast.  So I eat that way for 4 days in a row Mon-Thurs.  
On Friday-Sunday,  I do a 72 hr fast.  I drink green tea (plain), water and salt for those 72 hrs.  
Then the next Monday I do the OMAD with the two hour window.  
So It's a 72 hr fast every week with a strict OMAD for 4 days.  
I hike my hilly trails on my property and do some resistance training on my arms and abs.  That is my only exercise.  
Yes,  it is extreme,  but after almost 3 yrs of very little visceral fat coming off my waist and weight stalls,  it was time to get serious.  
I'm finally seeing progress.  I figured I will do this extreme fasting for another 60 days or until my visceral gut fat is at a healthy size,  then I will do the OMAD for the normal 7 days a week. 
I'll keep you updated on how long it takes.  
But I wanted it bad enough to finally get extreme.

top_comments.text:
I believe there may be some contradictions in the message being shared, particularly around encouraging people to consume fat and carbohydrates (especially sugars) without clearly explaining the underlying science.

From my understanding of more than a year of research, the human body is capable of using fat as a highly efficient source of energy, and many people who follow higher-fat, low to non-carbohydrate approaches report sustained energy levels during physical activity like gymming. Some studies also suggest that individuals training on higher-fat diets may experience improved endurance compared to those relying on sugar-based fuels.

It is also important to consider the role of sugar and highly processed foods in cardiovascular health. While fats themselves are not inherently harmful, excessive intake of refined sugars and processed foods has been linked to metabolic issues and changes in cholesterol particles, including the formation of Small Dense LDL particles(SDL/Oxalated LDL) that are associated with increased cardiovascular risk. Other contributing factors, such as smoking and poor dietary habits, can further increase these risks.

My intention in raising this point is not to criticize, but to encourage careful review of the available research before sharing health-related content. Providing well-supported, balanced information helps people make informed decisions about their health and well-being.

top_comments.text:
1. Microbiome Adaptation (The "Dead" Bacteria)
The gut microbiome is highly adaptive and operates on a "use it or lose it" principle.
Specialization: When carbohydrates are removed for an extended period, the specific strains of bacteria (such as Prevotella) that ferment fiber and starch diminish due to a lack of fuel.
Consequence: If carbohydrates are suddenly reintroduced, the gut lacks the necessary microbial workforce to process them. This leads to malabsorption, localized inflammation, and significant digestive distress as the "wrong" bacteria attempt to ferment the new fuel source.
2. Pancreatic and Enzyme Regulation
The body regulates enzyme production based on consistent dietary intake.
Amylase Downregulation: The pancreas produces amylase specifically to break down starches into glucose. In a sustained absence of carbs, amylase production drops significantly.
Metabolic Shift: When a high-carb load hits the system after a long hiatus, the pancreas is "caught off guard." This results in a slower-than-normal breakdown of the food, leaving it to sit in the digestive tract longer, causing the reported "sick" feeling.
3. Osmotic Shifts and Glycogen Rehydration
The "ballooning" effect mentioned is a physical law of biochemistry involving glycogen storage.
The 4-to-1 Ratio: Carbohydrates are stored in the liver and muscles as glycogen. Every 1 gram of glycogen requires approximately 3 to 4 grams of water to be stored alongside it.
The Rebound: In a state of ketosis or carnivore, glycogen stores are depleted. Upon eating carbs, the body aggressively refills these "tanks." A person storing 500g of glycogen will automatically pull in 1.5kg to 2kg (roughly 3–4 lbs) of water weight almost overnight. This is often mistaken for fat gain, but it is actually intracellular and systemic water retention.
4. Physiological Insulin Resistance
When the body is adapted to burning fat (fat-adapted), it undergoes a process called Physiological Insulin Resistance (also known as Adaptive Glucose Sparing).
The Mechanism: The muscles temporarily "refuse" glucose to save it for the brain.
The Impact: If a high-carb load is introduced during this state, blood sugar remains elevated for much longer than usual because the muscles are not yet "awake" to the insulin signal. This prolonged high blood sugar causes systemic inflammation and lethargy.
What is Metabolic Flexibility?
Metabolic Flexibility is the body's ability to efficiently switch between burning different fuel sources—specifically fat (ketones) and sugar (glucose)—based on availability and demand.
A "flexible" person can burn fat during a fast or low-carb period, but when they eat a carb-heavy meal, their body quickly switches gears to burn that glucose without significant inflammation or "ballooning."
When you stay strict carnivore for too long, you can actually lose flexibility because the "carb-burning" machinery goes dormant.
How to Lose the Weight Again: Two Options
Option 1: The Strict Carnivore Flush
This is the fastest way to drop the water weight and "reset" the system.
The Action: Return immediately to zero carbs (meat, salt, and water only).
The Result: As soon as the body burns through the newly stored glycogen, the kidneys will receive the signal to drop the associated 4-to-1 water weight. This typically happens within 3 to 5 days.
Key: You must be aggressive with water and salt intake to help the kidneys flush the inflammation.
Option 2: Low Carb & Metabolic Flexibility Training
This is a slower approach that "retrains" the body to handle carbs without the massive rebound.
The Action: Stay at under 50g of carbs per day using clean sources (berries or squash).
The Strategy: Use Intermittent Fasting (2MAD) to ensure you are burning fat for 16+ hours a day, but include a small amount of carbs in your eating window.
The Result: This keeps the "amylase" and gut bacteria active enough that if you do stray from the diet, your body has the machinery ready to handle it. The weight loss is more gradual, but the "ballooning" effect becomes less severe over time as your metabolic flexibility increases.
